title: Effectiveness of a Generate–Verify–Repair Pipeline with Batfish for LLM‑Generated Vendor CLI Configurations
abstract: We report a preregistered paired experiment (cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1) that evaluated whether a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline—shared initial LLM candidate (gpt-5-mini) + a deterministic Batfish‑style validator + at most one automated LLM repair—reduces deterministic‑verifier detected semantic/safety failures on intent→vendor‑CLI tasks. Planned N=300 pairs; 266 complete pairs were analysed after preregistered exclusions. Baseline pass-rate = 260/266 (97.744%); guarded (final GVR) pass-rate = 265/266 (99.624%). Paired difference = 0.01879699248; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0625. Paired bootstrap (B=10,000, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0037593984962406013, 0.03759398496240601]. Repair was invoked for 6 tasks; median repair iterations per task = 0. Per‑episode latency was not recorded in per‑task artifacts and thus could not be evaluated. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the observed absolute improvement is small and did not meet the preregistered α=0.05 decision rule. We present preregistered design details, deterministic validator semantics, complete numeric outcomes, representative artifact‑grounded repair examples, contamination findings (no exact public duplicates flagged), and an evidence‑grounded discussion of limitations and implications.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being applied to NetOps tasks such as intent→CLI translation, zero‑touch configuration synthesis, and automated maintenance workflows [1,2]. Stochastic generation can produce syntactic or semantic violations—missing commands, unsafe ordering, or constraint breaches—that create operational risk when applied to device CLIs. To mitigate those risks, research prototypes interpose deterministic verifiers (e.g., Batfish or header‑space analyses) and bounded repair loops—generate–verify–repair (GVR)—so that only outputs passing a deterministic oracle are accepted [3–5]. Prior art documents component designs and small prototypes, but preregistered, paired evaluations that instrument verifier‑triggered repair with archived deterministic traces are limited [1–4].

Motivated by this gap, we preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study to answer: Does a GVR pipeline that uses a single sampled initial LLM candidate per task (shared_initial_candidate semantics), a deterministic Batfish‑style validator, and at most one automated LLM repair call reduce verifier‑detected semantic/safety failures relative to the same initial candidate without repair? Our contribution is a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired evaluation that (a) preserves shared_initial_candidate semantics per the registration, (b) records deterministic validator traces for each episode, (c) reports exact paired contingency counts and inferential tests, and (d) provides representative artifact‑grounded repair examples and reproducibility metadata.
sections.related_work:
Prior evaluations of LLMs for network configuration focus on translation quality and prototype automation [1]. Surveys synthesize failure modes and advocate grounding with retrieval, deterministic validators, or tool augmentation for safety [2]. Generate–verify–repair architectures have been proposed in regulated code and other domains to achieve deterministic validation via external oracles and bounded repair loops [3]. Batfish and header‑space analyses provide deterministic reachability and ordering checks and are frequently proposed as verifier components for LLM‑augmented NetOps pipelines [4]. Empirical analyses emphasizing sequence and vendor‑syntax difficulties motivate verifier augmentation when LLMs synthesize router configurations [5].

This study differs by executing a preregistered, paired test that (i) fixes the initial sampled candidate shared across arms, isolating the effect of the validator‑triggered repair step; (ii) archives per‑episode validator traces and provider call accounting; and (iii) reports both exact McNemar inference and a paired bootstrap CI to clarify finite‑sample behavior when discordant counts are small.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The study preregistration (cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1; preregistration SHA‑256: 46a223492f760950b3d06f475129ce21e52e296c4c2a1e09df3ccd50bec9f891) specified a paired confirmatory design with shared_initial_candidate generation semantics. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where the same single sampled initial model candidate per task yields (1) the baseline outcome (single‑shot candidate → deterministic validator pass/fail) and (2) the guarded outcome (same candidate → validator; if it fails, at most one automated LLM repair call is permitted and the final verifier pass/fail is recorded). This estimand isolates the effect of the allowed validator‑triggered repair for a fixed initial candidate.

Task bank and sampling: The preregistered task bank deterministically generated 300 intent→CLI pairs (150 Cisco‑like; 150 Juniper‑like) combining public NetConfEval‑style examples and a seeded synthetic generator. Generation seeds, generator id, and task manifests are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Inclusion/exclusion, retry, and missingness rules were applied as preregistered; 34 both‑arm provider/infrastructure failures were excluded by deterministic rules, leaving 266 complete paired units for the primary analysis (analysis/missingness_summary.csv).

Model, orchestration, and sampling disclosure: Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json: declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). Archived configuration fields include max_output_tokens = 1024, maximum_attempts_per_call = 1, provider = openai_responses, and temperature = null (unset). The orchestration adapter was hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Provider‑call accounting (deterministic_reconciliation.json) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 306 with 34 failed calls; repair stage calls recorded = 6. Because temperature was archived as null and no deterministic sampling seed is present, nondeterministic sampling of model outputs cannot be excluded for recorded provider calls; we explicitly report this in the Disclosure Statement.

Deterministic validator semantics and scoring: The binary oracle was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. For each episode the validator executed: CLI syntactic parsing and normalization; per‑task required‑sequence checks (expected_sequence vs parsed commands); constrained‑field touch checks (allowed_fields and allowed_touched_fields); and reachability/constraint validation on the synthetic topology model. Episode artifacts include validation_before and validation_after traces listing parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation codes, and a normalized_configuration string. The validator’s boolean pass/fail is used for the primary endpoint and is archived in execution/scoring/*.json.

Repair loop and shared_initial_candidate mechanics: The preregistered repair policy permits at most one automated LLM repair call for a failed initial candidate. Repair prompts include the validator’s failure codes and the task constraints; repair provider traces and repaired candidate artifacts are archived when invoked. The bounded (≤1) repair design models a constrained automated correction before human escalation and is a preregistered design choice.

Analysis and inferential methods: The primary confirmatory test was the exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary outcomes (α=0.05). For interval estimation we used a paired bootstrap percentile CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) for the paired difference. Missingness handling followed the preregistration (complete_pair_primary): pairs with both‑arm provider failures were excluded from the primary analysis (34 excluded pairs); sensitivity analyses treated excluded pairs conservatively as failures to test robustness. All analysis artifacts and code were run by paired_binary_analysis_v1 and are archived (analysis/*).
sections.results:
Execution accounting and missingness: Planned episodes = 600 (300 pairs × 2); completed episodes = 532; failed episodes = 68. Complete paired units analysed = 266; both_missing_pairs = 34 excluded per preregistration (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Provider and model call accounting (deterministic_reconciliation.json) reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 306, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 272, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 34, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 272, and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 300, repair: 6}.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 266): baseline successes = 260; guarded final successes = 265. Paired contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 260, n10 = 5, n01 = 0, n00 = 1. Observed proportions: baseline = 260/266 = 0.9774436090; guarded = 265/266 = 0.9962406015. Paired difference = 0.01879699248. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0625 (preregistered α=0.05 decision rule: not significant). Paired bootstrap percentile CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) = [0.0037593984962406013, 0.03759398496240601] (analysis_log.jsonl).

Interpretation of discordant counts and inferential tension: The exact McNemar test depends only on discordant counts (n10 and n01) and yields discrete p‑values when discordants are few; here (n10=5, n01=0) p=0.0625. The bootstrap CI, which summarizes resampled paired‑difference variability, narrowly excludes zero. This difference is expected in small‑discordant settings and does not indicate an analysis error—both inferential outputs are reported to aid reader judgment on practical relevance versus formal hypothesis acceptance.

Repair behavior and representative artifacts: Repair was invoked 6 times of 300 tasks; median repair iterations per task = 0. Representative artifact: task‑000008 (execution/responses/task-000008-shared-initial.txt, sha256 = 89306095ceeedc3df7d752beb035f342edf9e82b7252e45356919e29958245e7) shows the shared initial candidate terminated with an incomplete final line "interface uplink2\n" and was invalid per validation_before. The guarded final artifact (execution/responses/task-000008-guarded.txt, sha256 = d52b7616f93a608409c7ce4eeb21958b8ceeb502faaf302d9b36468d8a627944) contains the corrected complete sequence and passed validation_after. All episode validator traces document concrete failure codes that triggered repair and the normalized_configuration that the validator accepted post‑repair (execution/scoring/task-000008-*.json).

Contamination and sensitivity checks: analysis/contamination_summary.csv contains no exact public duplicates (no tasks excluded for contamination in the primary analysis). Sensitivity treating the 34 excluded both‑arm episodes as failures (conservative N=300 analysis) yields baseline = 260/300 = 0.866667 and guarded = 265/300 = 0.883333; the discordant counts remain n10=5, n01=0 and exact McNemar p = 0.0625, confirming that the primary inferential conclusion is robust to the preregistered conservative missingness handling.

Archival artifacts and reproducibility primitives: Key archived artifacts used in reporting include execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256: 34fe154dde2a540fdf6b3132182eace8dbf9dc10a600d8cffebb3bf4e68d8449), execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha256: 88b650861f5d11cfcd2031d7c810b266fe2066b18d3a4c5b08d246810d3923ab), analysis/condition_summary.csv (sha256: ca455160c53ff3ae4e6e9d57440df8cb21f78c03ed97dee6f0bed94eb421e16e), and deterministic_reconciliation.json (analysis hash: 32ea4be9caac88b78993caafec4ac323b8b822f1b6813e0e3747f3144e7a4490). These artifacts provide full episode scoring, provider call accounting, and paired contingency data used in the confirmatory analysis.
sections.discussion:
Statistical and operational interpretation: The guarded GVR pipeline produced a small absolute increase in validator pass‑rate (~1.88 percentage points). Under the preregistered exact‑McNemar decision rule the improvement did not reach α=0.05 (p=0.0625). The bootstrap CI excluding zero indicates a small positive effect estimate but does not supplant the preregistered test. Practically, given the high baseline first‑pass accuracy (~97.7%), few failures were available for repair to correct, limiting the observable benefit of bounded automated repair in this corpus.

Design lessons grounded in artifacts: (1) High baseline pass rates reduce statistical power to detect repair benefits in a bounded‑repair design; preregistered power planning should anticipate baseline difficulty or increase N. (2) The repair stage executed rarely (6 repair calls recorded), so future evaluations should include alternative arms (e.g., independent multi‑draw sampling, constrained first‑pass prompting) to compare strategies—noting that such arms were not preregistered or executed here. (3) Per‑episode latency was not archived in per‑task artifacts and thus the preregistered latency hypothesis (median ≤ 60 s) could not be evaluated; future runs must record per‑episode timing to validate operational bounds.

Threats to validity: Internal validity: the shared_initial_candidate estimand measures the effect of validator‑triggered repair for a fixed initial sample and does not evaluate independent multiple draws or constrained prompting (those were not executed under the preregistration). Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite rule battery (syntactic normalization, required‑sequence checks, allowed_field constraints, and topology‑based reachability) and may miss semantic violations outside those rules. External validity: tasks derive from public NetConfEval‑style examples and a seeded synthetic generator limited to two vendor clusters; results may not generalize to other vendors, larger production topologies, or workloads with different difficulty distributions. Conclusion validity: few discordant pairs (n10=5, n01=0) and excluded provider failures reduced precision.

Operational implications (bounded and conditional): The data suggest that in settings where first‑pass LLM accuracy is already high, adding a bounded automated repair stage yields only modest incremental verifier pass‑rate improvements. By contrast, when first‑pass accuracy is lower, GVR may produce larger absolute gains. Importantly, these implications are conditional on the validator’s coverage: if the verifier lacks coverage for key semantic failure modes, GVR cannot correct undetected errors. We therefore recommend combining broader verifier rule coverage with explicit latency and throughput instrumentation in follow‑on studies.

Reproducibility and auditability: All execution and analysis artifacts referenced above are archived with SHA‑256 manifests and are sufficient to reproduce the confirmatory paired contingency and McNemar calculations. The archival includes the initial shared responses (execution/responses/*), per‑episode validator traces (execution/scoring/*.json), provider call traces for shared generations and repairs (execution/provider_calls/*), and reconciliation manifests (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). Reviewers asked for conventional IEEE bibliography formatting; we present verified numbered citations in text and provide the corresponding verified record identifiers in the cited_record_ids field for bibliographic assembly.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired study of a GVR pipeline (gpt‑5‑mini + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + ≤1 automated repair) on intent→CLI tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics, the guarded pipeline improved verifier pass‑rate by 0.01879699248 but did not meet the preregistered exact‑McNemar α=0.05 decision rule (p=0.0625). A paired bootstrap CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) narrowly excludes zero. Repair calls were rare (6/300) and median repair iterations per task = 0. Per‑episode latency was not archived and could not be assessed. The results are evidence‑grounded and limited to the preregistered estimand and task corpus; they suggest modest gains from a bounded automated repair stage when baseline first‑pass accuracy is high and highlight the need to record latency and broaden verifier coverage in future studies.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure (concise): Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json archived; declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Preregistration: cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1 (manifest SHA‑256: 46a223492f760950b3d06f475129ce21e52e296c4c2a1e09df3ccd50bec9f891). Human role and autonomy boundary: before the autonomy lock a human Research Director selected the topic family and approved pre‑lock infrastructure development; after the autonomy lock the registered pipeline autonomously performed literature selection, preregistration, experimental execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, AI peer review simulation, and revision. Nondeterminism disclosure: archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset) and no deterministic sampling seed is archived; therefore nondeterministic sampling of model outputs cannot be excluded for the recorded provider calls. Execution and analysis artifacts, logs, and hash manifests cited in the paper are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the preregistration for audit per the track’s reproducibility requirements.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: both arms used the same single sampled initial candidate per preregistration; the estimand measures validator‑triggered repair benefit for that fixed initial sample and does not evaluate independent first‑pass generations or constrained first‑pass prompting strategies.

Missingness and sample reduction: planned N=300 pairs; after infrastructure/provider exclusions 266 pairs were complete and 34 both‑arm episodes were excluded per preregistered rules, reducing effective sample size and precision.
Small discordant counts: primary inference used exact McNemar with few discordants (n10=5, n01=0); conclusions are sensitive to inferential choice and limited power.
Validator coverage: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite set of syntactic/semantic/reachability rules; semantic violations outside its coverage are possible and unmeasured.

Runtime nondeterminism and sampling: archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null and no deterministic seed; nondeterministic sampling cannot be excluded for recorded model calls.
H2 latency not evaluated: per‑episode end‑to‑end latency was not present in archived per‑task artifacts and therefore the preregistered latency bound (median ≤ 60 s) could not be assessed.

External validity: task corpus derives from public NetConfEval‑style examples and a seeded synthetic generator limited to two vendor‑dialect clusters; results do not imply universal benefit across other vendors, larger topologies, or production deployments.
